hood_landmark.Fitzroy: Brunswick Street's bars, vintage shops and street art
hood_landmark.St Kilda: Luna Park's heritage amusement rides beside St Kilda Pier
hood_landmark.Carlton: Lygon Street's Little Italy beside the UNESCO-listed Royal Exhibition Building
hood_landmark.Southbank: Southbank Promenade's riverside dining below the Eureka Skydeck
hood_landmark.Richmond: The MCG stadium on its doorstep and Victoria Street's Vietnamese eateries

avoid.reason: Late-night alcohol-fuelled rowdiness around King Street clubs and some CBD corners; keep an eye on belongings on crowded trams.

hood_desc: Fitzroy is Melbourne's bohemian creative hub with vintage shops, street art, live music and buzzing Brunswick Street bars, perfect for hip young travelers and night owls.
St Kilda is the bayside beach suburb with a seaside promenade, Luna Park, cake shops and lively nightlife, great for beachgoers and backpackers.
Carlton is the historic Italian quarter around Lygon Street, home to Melbourne University, classic cafes and pasta restaurants, suited to students and food lovers.
Southbank is the polished riverside precinct of arts venues, casino, high-rise hotels and Yarra promenade dining, ideal for luxury and first-time visitors.
Richmond is a trendy, gritty-chic inner suburb with Vietnamese eateries on Victoria Street, hip pubs and boutiques, appealing to foodies and younger travelers.

water.note: Tap water is treated and safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: Contactless bank cards and phones are now accepted on trams, with rollout continuing across the network; otherwise use a myki card (AU$6, ~US$4) from station machines, 7-Elevens or as a mobile myki in your phone wallet. Fares cap at about AU$11-12 (~US$8) a day for unlimited travel. Trams within the CBD's Free Tram Zone cost nothing.
transit.hours: Trains and trams run roughly 5am-midnight, with 24-hour Night Network service on Friday and Saturday nights.

transit.m: SkyBus City Express to Southern Cross Station (30 min)

food.name: Chicken parma
food.desc: The Victorian pub staple: crumbed chicken schnitzel under napoli sauce, ham and melted cheese, served with chips and salad and a pot of beer.

places.name: The Court House Hotel
places.note: Classic corner pub with a parma regularly ranked among the city's best.

places.name: The Precinct Hotel
places.note: Big pub plates and a loyal local following on match days.

places.name: The Duke of Wellington
places.note: Melbourne's oldest pub licence; a central spot for the full parma ritual.

food.name: Dim sims and dumplings
food.desc: The Melbourne-born dim sim is a fat pork-and-cabbage parcel, steamed or deep fried; Chinatown adds soup dumplings and hand-pulled noodles.

places.name: South Melbourne Market
places.note: The market dim sim stall has been frying and steaming since the 1940s.

places.name: HuTong Dumpling Bar
places.note: Chinatown institution for xiao long bao folded in the window.

places.name: Camy Shanghai Dumpling Restaurant
places.note: Cash-only, no-frills, famously cheap plates of pork dumplings.

food.name: Souvlaki
food.desc: Melbourne has one of the biggest Greek populations outside Greece; late-night souvlaki wrapped with chips, tomato and tzatziki is the proof.

places.name: Stalactites
places.note: Open around the clock since 1978 under its famous fake stalactite ceiling.

places.name: Hella Good
places.note: Stalactites' owners took over the Fitzroy souvlaki shop; same handheld format.

places.name: Kalimera Souvlaki Art
places.note: Melbourne Greek heartland; pork gyros wrapped with chips and paprika tzatziki.

food.name: Banh mi in Footscray
food.desc: Melbourne's Vietnamese west turns out crackly baguettes filled with pork, pate, pickled carrot, coriander and chilli for the price of a coffee.

places.name: Nhu Lan Bakery
places.note: The benchmark pork roll; expect a queue at lunchtime, and it moves fast.

places.name: N. Lee Bakery
places.note: Victoria Street favourite doing crisp rolls and Vietnamese pastries.

places.name: Footscray Market
places.note: Bakeries and stalls all around the market for rolls, pho and sugarcane juice.

food.name: Melbourne brunch
food.desc: The city that exported smashed avocado treats breakfast as a serious meal: eggs, house bread, ferments and a properly made coffee.

places.name: Higher Ground
places.note: Soaring former powerstation dining room; the flagship of the brunch scene.

places.name: Top Paddock
places.note: Produce-driven all-day menu that helped define the Melbourne brunch look.

places.name: Industry Beans
places.note: Roastery cafe pairing coffee flights with inventive breakfast plates.

food.name: Lygon Street Italian
food.desc: Carlton's Little Italy has fed Melbourne pasta, pizza and espresso since the 1950s, and much of the strip is still family run.

places.name: Tiamo
places.note: Old-school red-sauce trattoria on Lygon Street, unchanged for decades.

places.name: DOC Pizza & Mozzarella Bar
places.note: Wood-fired Neapolitan pizza and burrata flown in weekly.

places.name: Pellegrini's Espresso Bar
places.note: 1954 espresso bar; granita, spaghetti and a bar stool at the counter.

food.name: Flat white
food.desc: Melbourne treats coffee as a craft: single-origin espresso under silky milk, poured in laneway bars by roasters who source their own beans.

places.name: Patricia Coffee Brewers
places.note: Standing-room-only laneway bar; no food, no wi-fi, just excellent coffee.

places.name: Market Lane Coffee
places.note: Seasonal single origins served beside the market since 2009.

places.name: Proud Mary
places.note: Roastery cafe known for rare lots and a busy all-day food menu.

food.name: Victorian craft beer
food.desc: Melbourne's northern suburbs are stacked with breweries and beer bars pouring pale ales, lagers and sours brewed on site.

places.name: Stomping Ground Brewing Co
places.note: Big beer hall in an old textile factory with a rotating tap list.

places.name: Moon Dog World
places.note: Tropical-themed mega brewpub with a lagoon and dozens of taps.

places.name: Carwyn Cellars
places.note: Bottle shop and tap room that curates the best of Victorian brewing.

landmarks: Federation Square
Melbourne's civic heart, a bold fractal-patterned architectural complex that's the city's main gathering and event space.
Flinders Street Station
The iconic yellow-domed Edwardian railway station facade that anchors classic Melbourne street photography.
Royal Exhibition Building
A grand 19th-century UNESCO World Heritage building set in the lush Carlton Gardens.
Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG)
Australia's largest and most storied sports stadium, a pilgrimage site for cricket and AFL fans.
St Paul's Cathedral
A neo-Gothic cathedral with striking spires standing directly across from Flinders Street Station.
Queen Victoria Market
A historic open-air market and Melbourne institution, vibrant with produce stalls, food, and street life.
Eureka Tower / Skydeck
One of the world's tallest residential towers, its Skydeck 88 observation deck gives sweeping views over Melbourne and Port Phillip Bay.
Royal Botanic Gardens Melbourne
Sprawling world-class gardens with lakes and diverse plantings, a green escape minutes from the CBD.
St Kilda Beach & Luna Park
A beloved seaside strip with a historic 1912 amusement park entrance and views of the St Kilda Pier.
Shrine of Remembrance
A monumental war memorial atop a hill, offering formal ceremonial architecture and skyline views down Anzac Avenue.

train.note: Australia has no international trains. From Southern Cross Station, V/Line runs regional trains across Victoria, NSW TrainLink's XPT heads to Sydney (day service plus an overnight train with sleepers), and Journey Beyond's 'The Overland' crosses to Adelaide (journeybeyondrail.com.au) - a scenic once-or-twice-weekly service rather than everyday transport.

bus.note: No international coaches - Australia is an island continent. Long-distance buses use the Southern Cross coach terminal: Firefly Express (fireflyexpress.com.au) runs overnight to Adelaide and Sydney, while V/Line coaches and Greyhound Australia (greyhound.com.au) cover regional and interstate routes.

ferry.note: No international ferries. The Spirit of Tasmania (spiritoftasmania.com.au) sails to Devonport in Tasmania - a domestic crossing that now departs from Geelong, about an hour southwest of Melbourne, rather than from Melbourne itself. Book vehicle and cabin space well ahead in summer.

half.name: Great Ocean Road
half.blurb: Iconic coastal drive past the Twelve Apostles sea stacks, surf beaches and rainforest.

half.name: Phillip Island
half.blurb: Famous for its nightly penguin parade, rugged coastline and abundant wildlife encounters.

half.name: Yarra Valley
half.blurb: Cool-climate wine country dotted with cellar doors, produce and rolling green hills.

half.name: Mornington Peninsula
half.blurb: Coastal region blending beaches, wineries and steaming natural hot springs among the vines.

half.name: Dandenong Ranges
half.blurb: Misty forested hills with towering ferns, gardens and the historic Puffing Billy railway.

half.name: Ballarat
half.blurb: Grand gold-rush town with heritage streetscapes and the Sovereign Hill living-history site.
